topic: Anatomy of Dicot and Monocot Stems
title: Ring or Scattered Bundles? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
A sunflower stem, a maize stalk and the tough threads left after you chew sugarcane. Aarav stops at a sugarcane juice cart and asks why those hard threads are spread all through the cane.

You will read a young sunflower stem layer by layer: epidermis with cuticle and trichomes, collenchyma hypodermis, cortex, the starch sheath, half-moon pericycle patches, medullary rays, pith and one conjoint, open bundle. Then the xylem of a stem being built (endarch, protoxylem towards the pith) and a maize bundle with its sclerenchyma sheath, no cambium and a water cavity. Then dicot vs monocot stems side by side, a pause and think check, a worked sorting example, the endarch vs exarch exam trap, an original NEET match the following question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to answer. This is Episode 53 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE), PUC (Karnataka) and NEET students.
